name: Vermilion
poem: Ground from cinnabar and mercury — the violent, brilliant red that lacquered emperors and slowly poisoned the alchemists who chased it.

recipe.note: A vivid, fiery red leaning warmly toward orange.

lenses.label: Art History
lenses.intro: Ground from cinnabar for over two thousand years — the brightest, most dangerous red available to painters until the 20th century.

entries.title: The Birth of Venus
entries.blurb: Vermilion brushed onto Venus's lips and the folds of the cloak Zephyr blows — the warmest red Florentine workshops could produce.

entries.title: Carved Cinnabar Lacquer
entries.blurb: Layer upon layer of mercury-sulfide lacquer built up over months, then carved away to reveal landscapes and dragons in deep cinnabar relief.

entries.title: No. 14 (Reds)
entries.blurb: Rothko reached repeatedly for the brightest reds — the same family of pigments Hokusai used — to stage colour as pure emotional event.

lenses.label: Fashion
lenses.intro: A colour reserved for those who could survive being looked at — clergy, royalty, the operatic.

entries.title: The Cardinal's Mozzetta
entries.blurb: Cardinals wear the pigment of martyrdom — a deep vermilion silk cape worn over the rochet, signifying willingness to spill blood for the faith.

entries.title: The Hermès Box
entries.blurb: The exact orange-vermilion of the Hermès box was chosen out of necessity in WWII — the only colour cardboard the firm could source.

entries.title: The Chinese Wedding Qípáo
entries.blurb: Red for joy, fertility, warding off evil — a Chinese bride changes into a vermilion-red gown to be carried across the threshold of her new life.

lenses.label: Nature
lenses.intro: Cinnabar's deep red sits at the seam where geology turns into chemistry — beautiful, useful, and quietly venomous.

entries.title: Cinnabar Crystals
entries.blurb: The mineral source of vermilion — heavy, glassy red crystals found around volcanic vents. Grinding them releases mercury vapour.

entries.title: The Northern Cardinal
entries.blurb: The brilliant red comes from carotenoids in the bird's diet — what it eats, it wears. Captive birds fade to dusty pink within a season.

entries.title: The Strawberry Poison-Dart Frog
entries.blurb: Aposematic colouration — the brighter the red, the more toxic the skin. Indigenous hunters tipped blowdarts with the frog's secretions.

lenses.label: Pop Culture
lenses.intro: Vermilion is the colour brands reach for when they want to be seen first — and remembered.

entries.title: The London Phone Box
entries.meta: K2 kiosk · Sir Giles Gilbert Scott, 1924
entries.blurb: Painted vermilion red to be spotted in fog — a design so iconic the boxes are now Grade II listed even as the phones inside go silent.

entries.title: Coca-Cola Red
entries.blurb: The exact red was chosen to match the barrels Coca-Cola syrup shipped in — vermilion-adjacent and now arguably the most replicated colour on Earth.

entries.title: Holi Festival Powders
entries.blurb: Crowds throw clouds of vermilion gulal — once made from herbs, now mostly synthetic — turning streets and skin the colour of celebration.

lenses.label: Etymology
lenses.intro: The colour's many names trace its travels — mercury, worms, alchemy, empire.

entries.title: "Vermiculus"
entries.blurb: Originally named for a different red — kermes, made from crushed scale insects. The pigment from cinnabar inherited the name when worm-red faded from use.

entries.title: "Cinnabar"
entries.blurb: The Greeks borrowed the word from Persian, where it described the same mineral. By the Roman period both pigment and name moved freely across the Mediterranean.

entries.title: "Zhū" (朱)
entries.blurb: The character for vermilion also means "crimson" and "the emperor's edit" — imperial decrees were brushed in cinnabar ink as a mark of authority.

lenses.label: Symbolism
lenses.intro: A colour that means power in almost every culture, but disagrees on what power feels like.

entries.title: The Imperial Seal
entries.blurb: Only the emperor was permitted to mark documents in vermilion ink — a single red stroke that turned a draft into law.

entries.title: The Torii Gate
entries.blurb: Painted vermilion to keep evil spirits out and lacquered with mercury sulfide to protect the wood — the colour itself is a barrier.

entries.title: Sindoor
entries.blurb: The line of vermilion powder a husband paints in his wife's hair parting — worn daily, renewed for life, a mark of being claimed by love.
